name: swift-nanohttp
description: A small, dependency-free HTTP/1.1 server framework in Swift for macOS, iOS and tvOS. Run a web server inside your app or tool: routing, JSON, forms and uploads, file serving, cookies and WebSockets, plus an HTML builder. Safe defaults (loopback only, limits, timeouts) and an option to run everything on one thread.

paragraphs: NanoHTTP is a small, extensible HTTP/1.1 server framework for macOS, iOS and tvOS. It runs a web server inside your own process, with routing, forms, uploads, file serving and WebSockets, and no dependencies. It is based on Swifter by Damian Kołakowski.

It is made for servers that are used by you, your own devices or a small trusted group: tools, local user interfaces, companion apps, test servers. It does not provide TLS or authentication, and it is not built to withstand many hostile clients; see Security.

Version 2.1 is the current version. Compared with 2.0 it adds deferred responses (a server that hands requests to other threads answers later), cookies, JSON responses from any Encodable value, a multipart parser that works on bytes, signal callbacks that can stop a server, and six runnable examples. Version 2.0 was a major release with a new API in many places, safer defaults and a faster server; if you come from 1.x, MIGRATION-2.0.md tells what to change. The CHANGELOG says what is new in every version.
